 Republican Mark Teixeira ahead in race for US House District 21
 KUT 90.5 | 
 By
 Olivia Aldridge 
 Published November 3, 2026 at 6:07 PM CST
 Updated November 3, 2026 at 9:03 PM CST 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 Kristin Hook and Mark Teixeira campaigns Kristin Hook, pictured at left, is running against Mark Teixeira for a seat in the U.S. House of Representatives. 
 As initial voting results become available, Republican Mark Teixeira appears to have a strong lead in the race to represent Texas' 21st congressional district. He is running against Democrat Kristin Hook . 
 Teixeira is favored to win the seat, which was previously held by Republican U.S. Rep. Chip Roy. Voters in the district have not elected a Democrat since 1978. The district includes a broad swath of the Texas Hill Country, covering portions of San Antonio and Austin. 
 Roy, a Republican who was first elected to the seat in 2018, decided to run for Texas attorney general this year instead. He lost to state Sen. Mayes Middleton during the primary runoff election. 
 Teixeira, a former Major League baseball player, has campaigned as a “conservative fighter” who will be tough on immigration and adhere to President Trump’s “America First” agenda. 
 Hook, a scientist making her second run for the TX-21 seat, sharply diverges from Trump on immigration issues and has run on a platform that includes opposing corporate interference in politics and protecting Texas natural resources, including water.
 Polls are open until 7 p.m. As long as you are in line by 7 p.m., you will be able to cast a ballot.
 Here's what you can expect in terms of election results: After the polls close at 7 p.m., early voting totals will come in first. Following that, results will continue to roll in throughout the night as local and state election authorities update them. Some races may not be decided until Wednesday morning.
